title: triad-sdk-credential-clarify-and-stream-iterator-simplify
author: Aisha Romero
description:
Motivation: Developers reported friction when wiring credentials and consuming streaming responses across our Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Differences in credential shape (token vs. token+meta) and an overly verbose async iterator surface made client code verbose and brittle. This PR harmonizes the credential contract, reduces ceremony for streaming consumers, and ships compatibility shims to avoid breaking existing users.

What this PR does (single-run summary): - Introduces a single canonical CredentialEnvelope shape used by all SDKs (token, expires_at, source) and documents the minimal fields required by transports. - Simplifies streaming async iterators: replaces multi-stage Start/Resume/Drain API with a single ergonomic AsyncStream/StreamHandle pair that supports pause/resume and structured progress events. - Adds language-specific ergonomic helpers: Python async generator adapter, TS AsyncIterable shim with backpressure hints, and Go StreamReader interface with Read/Close semantics. - Adds compatibility layers: legacy_cred_adapter in each SDK that maps older credential tuples to the canonical envelope; runtime guard rails to log deprecation warnings without breaking. - Updates SDK versions: python -> 2.13.0, typescript -> 1.28.0, go -> v1.9.0; bump artifacts and changelogs. - Small runtime change in the redwood runtime client: Accept both legacy token str and CredentialEnvelope JSON on the transport handshake to increase backward compatibility.

Testing and QA: - Unit tests added for envelope normalization across all three SDKs. - End-to-end smoke tests on streaming with pause/resume and token rotation simulated. - Backwards-compat regression tests verifying older token-only clients still connect and receive a deprecation warning (non-blocking). - Manual interoperability test matrix: py ts go cross-consume streaming generated sample payloads for 10k tokens.

Files touched (high-level): - sdk/python/redwood/auth.py (canonical envelope, legacy adapter) - sdk/python/redwood/streaming/async_stream.py (new AsyncStream adapter, examples) - sdk/python/pyproject.toml (version bump) - sdk/typescript/src/credentials/envelope.ts (canonical type + adapter) - sdk/typescript/src/stream/async_iterable_shim.ts - sdk/typescript/package.json (version bump) - sdk/go/credentials/envelope.go - sdk/go/stream/stream_reader.go - docs/sdk/migration/credential-envelope.md

Checklist: - [x] Define canonical credential envelope shape and update docs - [x] Implement adapters in Python/TS/Go - [x] Add unit + integration tests - [x] Update changelogs and bump versions - [x] Add runtime transport guard to accept both shapes - [x] Run cross-language interoperability smoke tests

Migration guidance (brief): Existing token-only integrations will continue to work. They will see a non-fatal deprecation warning in logs indicating the recommended envelope shape. To opt-in to richer telemetry and smoother rotation semantics, migrate to CredentialEnvelope { token, expires_at (RFC3339), source: string }. Examples and migration snippets are in docs/sdk/migration/credential-envelope.md.

Notes: - Kept the public API surface minimal: the new stream helpers are additive and ship behind a feature flag in Go (default enabled). - Left room to later unify retry presets with the credential lease logic (follow-up ENG-2102).

Merge notes: Squash merge; small follow-up hotfix PR planned to tweak log levels in the runtime transport layer if we observe noisy deprecation logs in staging.

diff_snippets:
--- a/sdk/python/redwood/auth.py
+++ b/sdk/python/redwood/auth.py
@@ -10,6 +10,28 @@
+class CredentialEnvelope(TypedDict):
+    token: str
+    expires_at: Optional[str]  # RFC3339
+    source: Optional[str]
+
+def normalize_credential(raw):
+    if isinstance(raw, str):
+        return CredentialEnvelope(token=raw, expires_at=None, source="legacy")
+    # existing dict shape allowed
+    return CredentialEnvelope(**raw)
review_comments: Miguel: Please clarify the lifetime semantics for expires_at (UTC vs local). Suggested note added to docs.
Aisha: expires_at is RFC3339 UTC; updated docs and tests to assert timezone-normalized comparisons.
Priya: TS shim looks good; can we add a small example for backpressure hints?
Aisha: Added example in async_iterable_shim.ts and e2e test referencing hinting behavior.
Evan: Go stream Read semantics are clear; prefer making feature flag opt-out rather than opt-in for Go users.

release_notes: SDKs: unify credential format across Python/TS/Go (CredentialEnvelope) and add ergonomic streaming adapters. Backwards compatible with legacy token strings; deprecation warnings will be emitted. Version bumps: python 2.13.0, typescript 1.28.0, go v1.9.0.
